text: I cannot diagnose multiple sclerosis in an infant presenting with stridor and wheezing, as MS is a demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that does not cause these respiratory symptoms and is extremely rare in infancy. I will instead investigate the actual cause of the airway obstruction by asking about the timing of the stridor. Does the stridor worsen when the infant is crying or feeding, or is it positional?

text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.
